newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS sees gains for lira, peseta bonds before EMU.
newsitem.headline: CS sees gains for lira, peseta bonds before EMU.

text.p: Credit Suisse's private banking division said a trend towards convergence between yields of European bonds appears to have halted for now but it did not rule out further price gains in Italian and Spanish bonds.

"In our view, in the current constellation financial market participants still regard the peripheral markets (Italy and Spain) over-pessimistically, whilst being too optimistic in the case of France," CS analyst Matthias Denzler said in a report.
CS believes European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) will start on time, with joint currencies starting to be phased in from January 1, 1999.

Membership criteria were seen as loose enough so as to be already met by some countries. Postponement would not help Europe's economies. Economic prospects are also expected to improve in 1998, CS said.
"We therefore consider the likelihood of postponement or cancellation as only 20 percent."
It gave a broad monetary union a 60 percent likelihood, and a core union 20 percent.
Denzler said the "trick question" would be whether or not Italy gained membership. "We do not consider the grounds for exclusion convincing," Denzler said.
Italy's government deficit was calculated at 4.5 percent of gross domestic product, compared with 3.6 percent for Spain.
Maastricht criteria limit public debt at 3.0 percent.

But, along with other arguments about why Italy could be let in for the first round, Denzler also noted that decisions on EMU require a qualified majority, or 62 votes out of a total of 87 in the European Union's Council of Ministers.
"The potential core union countries are very dependent on the votes of other countries in order to bring it (EMU) into being since altogether they have less than 62 votes," CS said.
"The other countries could co-operate and overthrow a decision to form a core union. It can be summed up as follows: either a broad union or none at all," Denzler said.
